_note: Illustrative numbers: plausible and rounded, chosen so each lesson reads. Work is in units of about a millisecond of server time; capacity is units per second. The shapes are real (see GAME.md).

phones.label: Diners
phones.plain: Everyone on Forkcast right now, on their phones.

visitors.label: Visitors
visitors.plain: Everyone looking at the landing page right now. Each of their browsers asks for the page, and a server sends it back.

prototype.label: Prototype
prototype.term: a prototype on a self-hosted server
prototype.plain: Forkcast's first version, running on Aleister, Gilroy's server in the garage. Only Walter's testers can reach it.

feed.label: Photo feed
feed.plain: Photos of food, likes and follows. Every photo is stored forever.

landing.label: Landing
landing.plain: The page that explains Forkcast, with a box to join the waitlist. Static: the same files for everyone. Dynamic: built by our server for every visit.

backend.label: Backend
backend.plain: A rented server running our own code: it can build pages and take sign-ups.

signups_db.label: Postgres
signups_db.plain: A database of our own, here just to keep the waitlist.

form.label: Form
form.plain: Someone else's backend for forms: the page's sign-up box sends each sign-up there, and it keeps the list for us.

git.label: GitHub
git.plain: Every change saved as a commit, with the history kept on GitHub, so we can see what changed and go back to any commit.

garage_server.label: Aleister
garage_server.plain: Gilroy's server in the garage, running the app and the database together.

load_balancer.label: Balancer
load_balancer.plain: Hands each request to one of the servers, spreading the load.

postgres.label: Postgres
postgres.plain: The reservations book, run for you by the host.

redis.label: Redis
redis.plain: A nearby copy of recent answers, so the database isn't asked again and again.

cdn.label: CDN
cdn.plain: Copies of photos and scripts on servers close to diners.

queue.label: Queue
queue.plain: Work that can wait goes in a line; a worker gets through it.

model_api.label: Model API
model_api.plain: The AI model Forkcast asks, paid by the token.

dashboard.label: Board
dashboard.plain: The board's screen of numbers. Each tile is a question, asked again at every refresh.

replica.label: Replica
replica.plain: A read-only copy of the database that follows every change, for reads that would get in the way.

warehouse.label: Analytics
warehouse.plain: A separate database built for big questions. It stores each column together, so adding up millions of rows reads only what it needs. A copy job fills it.

scraper.label: HubbubBot
scraper.plain: Hubbub's machines, asking for every restaurant's tables at every time and party size, all night. Nobody else asks for those, so the cache never has them.

payments.label: Payments
payments.plain: Another company's computers, which take diners' deposits for us. We ask over the network, and wait for the answer.

repo.label: Melon's repo
repo.plain: Melon's copy of Forkcast's code on GitHub, open to anyone, with every version of every file he ever pushed.

package.label: keysafe-autoguard
package.plain: A package Aleister suggested: a stranger's code, installed on our server and run with its settings.

agent.label: Agent
agent.plain: The concierge, now able to act: it asks the model what to do, uses one of our app's tools (search, check a table, book), looks at the result, and asks again until the job's done.

index.label: Menu index
index.plain: Every restaurant's menu and allergy notes, stored as embeddings in our own Postgres, so the concierge can find the right ones and answer from them.
